regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein. Pertuzumab: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway. Trastuzumab: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Phesgo on Day 1 every 21 days after the chemotherapy component is complete; continue while beneficial and tolerated. This is active metastatic maintenance, not a fixed one-year adjuvant course.
key_points: Completed the chemotherapy component of dual HER2 treatment for metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable disease.

Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

After chemotherapy stops, use the agreed Phesgo maintenance plan (NCCP 00785 when eligible). Keep cardiac and response checks; chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics and growth factors do not automatically continue.

Echo or MUGA before starting and every 12 weeks during treatment, including maintenance. At an uninterrupted 21-day schedule, the first 12-week check is around cycle 5; count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose. A delay or route/phase change does not restart the clock. Cardiac concern may require 4–8-week checks or urgent earlier assessment.

Baseline imaging records the disease sites. ESMO recommends response review generally every 2–4 months, adjusted for symptoms, disease pace, sites and treatment. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis is used when appropriate; the team selects the actual scan and review date. Tumour markers may supplement assessment, not replace scans or determine a treatment change alone.

If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA when indicated. Repeat according to results, risk and the endocrine plan; DEXA is not a scan at each Phesgo cycle.

evidence_audit.coverage_summary: CLEOPATRA evaluated IV dual HER2 blockade with docetaxel in metastatic disease. Continuing HER2 treatment after chemotherapy is part of the strategy; this is not a separate randomised Phesgo-maintenance survival comparison. FeDeriCa compared the combined subcutaneous formulation with IV pertuzumab plus trastuzumab in early breast cancer. It met the primary pharmacokinetic non-inferiority endpoint, with similar pathological response and safety findings. It was not a trial proving identical survival for every chemotherapy backbone or metastatic sequence.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Shrink the cancer before surgery and contribute to reducing recurrence risk as part of a complete early-breast plan.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein. Docetaxel: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected. Carboplatin: Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen. Pertuzumab: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway. regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein. Paclitaxel: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues. Carboplatin: Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen. Pertuzumab: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway. Trastuzumab: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.

evidence_records.relevance_summary: FeDeriCa compared the combined subcutaneous formulation with IV pertuzumab plus trastuzumab in early breast cancer. It met the primary pharmacokinetic non-inferiority endpoint, with similar pathological response and safety findings. It was not a trial proving identical survival for every chemotherapy backbone or metastatic sequence.

drug_profiles.name: Phesgo
drug_profiles.mechanism: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein. Pertuzumab and trastuzumab bind different HER2 sites; the formulation includes hyaluronidase to support subcutaneous administration.
